name: North Ridge - West Side

pitch_detail.notes: Initial west rib pitches with good granite and vertical jointing; protection can be sparse. Loose blocks in approach gully; careful foot placement required.
Upper pitches to summit with steeper, more exposed climbing. Coarse granite with vertical jointing; the slab pitch has spaced protection. Quality varies; test holds. Final pitches near summit.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 3 down the north ridge.

rappel_detail.station: A small tree near the notch.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 3 of 3, then a short downclimb to a flat shoulder.
rappel_detail.station: A large block lower on the ridge.

rappels: 3 rappels down the north ridge - a small tree near the notch and a large block are two of the stations - plus a short downclimb to a flat shoulder
descent_text: The standard descent involves 3 rappels down the north ridge from the summit, or alternatively descend southwest with an 80-foot rappel. The granite offers good anchor possibilities through cracks and features, but careful placement is essential—test all anchors before committing weight. Be vigilant for loose blocks and flakes. Rope management is critical in low light. Once below technical terrain, descend gullies back toward the pass or PCT.
approach: Two primary approaches: (1) From the Cutthroat Lake trailhead on Highway 20, hike 1.8 miles with 500 feet elevation gain to Cutthroat Lake (4,800 ft). Continue another 3.7 miles with 1,800 feet elevation gain to Cutthroat Pass (6,800 ft), then follow the ridge crest south approximately 1 mile to the base of the North Ridge. (2) From Rainy Pass North trailhead (4,875 ft) on the PCT, hike about 1.5 miles north to just before Porcupine Creek (around 5,250 ft elevation), then ascend the ridge northeast toward Molar Tooth—approximately 2 miles with 2,300 feet elevation gain. The second gully provides a cleaner approach to the base of the north ridge and west rib.
overview: A moderate alpine route on Molar Tooth's north ridge featuring 2-3 low to moderate 5th class pitches up the west rib to the summit, with excellent granite climbing punctuated by loose rock hazards and quality variations.
beta: The North Ridge - West Side is one of the primary technical routes on Molar Tooth. The route ascends via the west rib with multiple short low 5th class pitches (up to 5.4), solid granite with vertical jointing, though protection is spaced in places, and enjoyable alpine climbing despite loose rock concerns. The descent via north ridge rappels requires careful anchor placement and rope management due to potential loose rock.
fa: Armstrong, Sandbo, Woodmansee, Apter, Gibson — July 1977
face: West Rib / West side of the North Ridge
